uncited: This family defines how scalar values are estimated at arbitrary query points within unstructured, hierarchically refined AMR datasets for volume rendering.
It solves the problem of mapping discrete, non-uniform cell data to continuous ray samples while maintaining visual continuity across level boundaries.

Unlike sibling methods that rely on virtual cells, surface propagation, or specific tree structures (e.g., [Adaptive Octree Construction](830-adaptive-octree-construction-with-2-1-balance-and-surface-pr.md), [TET-AMR](1094-tet-amr-data-structure.md)), this family focuses on the mathematical basis functions and temporal consistency required to stitch multi-level data seamlessly.
The simplest reconstruction strategy for AMR data, returning the scalar value of the leaf cell containing the query point.
The foundational concepts of AMR interpolation stem from the need to render unstructured grids efficiently on CPUs.
